rejected.title: Plotting points on the Cartesian plane
card: The Cartesian plane has a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis. They cross at the origin (0, 0). The axes split the plane into four quadrants.
A point is written as (x, y). Start at the origin. Move across first by x: right if positive, left if negative. Then move up or down by y: up if positive, down if negative.
Example: (−3, 2) means 3 units left, then 2 units up. The order matters, so (2, −3) is a different point. Any point on the x-axis has y = 0.
The rule y = x + 1 gives the points (0, 1), (1, 2) and (2, 3). Each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by the same amount, so the points sit on a straight line.
rejected.remember: Write (x, y): across first, then up or down.

a.q: Where is the point (4, −2) on the Cartesian plane?
a.why: The x-value 4 is positive, so move 4 units right. The y-value −2 is negative, so move 2 units down. Moving 2 units up would need a y-value of positive 2.
a.clue: Look at the sign of each number, x first.

b.q: Sam uses the rule y = 2x and finds the points (1, 2), (2, 4) and (3, 6). What does he see when he plots them?
opts: They lie on a straight line
They are scattered with no pattern
b.why: Each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by 2, the same amount every time, so the points form a straight line. They are not on the x-axis, because none of the y-values is 0.
b.clue: Check how y changes each time x goes up by 1.
